svg.aria-label: How ghost-infer runs a mixture-of-experts model bigger than the GPU: attention and shared weights go to the GPU, every expert stays in system RAM, the GPU's free memory caches the experts used most; cached experts run on the GPU and the rest on the CPU
svg.text: The model is split: what every token needs goes to the GPU, the experts stay in system RAM, and the GPU's free
memory caches the experts used most. Cached experts run on the GPU, the rest on the CPU. An 80B model runs on 8 GB.

g.text: Loading: attention and shared weights go to the GPU, every expert to system RAM
The GPU's free memory becomes an expert cache, filled from RAM
Token 1: 2 of its experts are cached and run on the GPU; 2 run on the CPU, in RAM
Token 2: 3 on the GPU, 1 on the CPU. That one keeps being used…
Token 3: …so it moved into the cache. Now all 4 run on the GPU

svg.text: Drawn small: real models have far more experts (Qwen3-Coder-Next has 512 a layer and uses 10 per token).
When even system RAM is too small, the experts that do not fit are read from the SSD as they are needed.
